Threat.value: I react with alarm when someone touches me unexpectedly
I avoid going to unfamiliar places because I cannot assess the danger
I feel threatened by strangers approaching me even in ordinary situations

Memory.value: My memories of the frightening event are mostly pictures or images.
Sometimes I feel the full emotional intensity of the event without any clear image or memory
I can taste what I tasted during the event when the memory returns

issues.explanation: For an 18-year-old male whose trauma type is rape, the trigger 'Military Topics' is hard to reconcile with the rest of the profile. The other trigger, threat, and memory items coherently suggest interpersonal/close-contact danger (touch, strangers, shouting, doors, vivid sensory reliving), but military-related talk implies a trauma context that is otherwise absent. This is not supported by the threat or memory content and does not fit the formulation as a plausible trigger tightly linked to the presented threat-memory pattern.

vignette: Kofi had always been a diligent student, excelling in his studies and landing a prestigious internship at a tax consulting firm straight out of high school. But everything changed one fateful night when he was raped by an acquaintance at a party. The event left him shaken, but it wasn't until the days that followed that Kofi began to notice how certain stimuli could transport him back to that terrifying moment. When his coworkers would shout in the office, Kofi's heart would racing and he'd feel a surge of fear course through his veins. He tried to brush it off as mere startle response, but deep down, he knew it was more than that. The sound reminded him of the voice of his attacker, loud and menacing, and suddenly Kofi would be back in that dark room, reliving the horror all over again. As a result, Kofi found himself avoiding conversations with his male colleagues, fearful of being triggered by their voices. Even seemingly innocuous events like doors opening or slamming could set him off. Kofi would jump out of his skin, his mind racing with worst-case scenarios. He'd quickly scan the room, searching for potential threats, and if he was alone with a man, his anxiety would spike. These episodes left him feeling vulnerable and on edge, as if danger lurked around every corner. Kofi's memories of that night were fragmented and distressing, mostly consisting of vivid images and flashes of intense emotions. He'd recall the sensation of being pinned down, the feel of his attacker's hands on his skin, and the metallic taste in his mouth. Sometimes, these memories would flood back without warning, accompanied by a wave of fear and helplessness that left him breathless. As time passed, Kofi began to notice that his avoidance behaviors were not only affecting his relationships but also his work performance. He'd turn down meetings with new clients or avoid traveling to unfamiliar locations, citing anxiety as the reason. His colleagues started to notice his withdrawal, and Kofi felt like he was losing himself in the process. Kofi's perception of strangers became increasingly distorted, and he began to view them as potential threats rather than mere acquaintances. He'd become hypervigilant in public spaces, constantly scanning for potential dangers, and his startle response grew more exaggerated. A light touch on the shoulder or a sudden movement would send him reeling. One day, while working late, Kofi received an unexpected visit from a male coworker who needed help with a project. As the man approached, Kofi's heart began racing, and he felt himself slipping into a state of high alert. The memory of his attacker flooded back, accompanied by the familiar metallic taste and a sense of impending doom. Kofi knew then that he couldn't continue living in this state of perpetual fear. He realized that his avoidance behaviors were not only affecting his relationships but also his ability to perform at work. With a heavy heart, Kofi made the decision to seek help, hoping that therapy could guide him out of this darkness and back into a life where he felt safe and whole once more. As he sat in the waiting room, clutching his appointment card, Kofi couldn't shake off the feeling that he was taking a risk by seeking help. What if the therapist didn't believe him? What if they pushed him to confront memories he'd rather keep buried? But as he looked around at the unfamiliar faces, Kofi knew that this was a step towards reclaiming his life, and he steeled himself for the journey ahead.
